name: elizaOS
tagline: A TypeScript runtime and product stack for autonomous AI agents
seoTitle: elizaOS - Open-Source TypeScript AI Agent Framework
metaDescription: elizaOS is an open-source TypeScript framework for autonomous AI agents: a model-agnostic plugin runtime plus the Eliza app, a CLI, and optional local inference.
overview: elizaOS is an open-source TypeScript framework and product stack for autonomous AI agents. The monorepo carries the core runtime, the Eliza end-user app, the elizaos CLI, cloud services, native bridges, and a set of first-party plugins, so you can either embed the runtime in your own code or run the finished agent application on top of it.

The framework is model-agnostic and extended entirely through plugins. @elizaos/core defines the AgentRuntime, the canonical types, the message loop, and the memory and state primitives, along with the plugin contracts themselves. A plugin exports a Plugin object that can register actions, providers, evaluators, services, model handlers, routes, events, tests, and app views — which is how capabilities such as messaging connectors, browser and desktop automation, calendar and inbox domains, and wallet operations are added rather than baked into the core.

Where the model runs is a routing decision, not a lock-in. The local-inference plugin provides an on-device path whose Eliza-1 registry contains 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B text tiers based on Gemma 4, plus local embeddings, speech, vision, and image-generation assets; hardware detection picks a supported backend, and eligible operations can run without a network connection once assets are downloaded. Eliza Cloud is optional and adds hosted model routing, deployment, and cross-device services, while direct model-provider configuration stays a first-class path. The bootable Linux and Android distributions live in a separate elizaOS/os repository.
features: Model-agnostic AgentRuntime in @elizaos/core with typed message loop, memory, and state primitives
Plugin contracts that register actions, providers, evaluators, services, model handlers, routes, events, tests, and app views
The elizaos CLI for scaffolding, upgrading, and deploying projects and plugins
Optional on-device inference via the Eliza-1 registry (2B/4B/9B/27B text tiers based on Gemma 4, plus embeddings, speech, vision, and image assets)
Per-capability routing between local, direct-provider, and Eliza Cloud backends
The Eliza app for web, desktop, and mobile, with chat, voice, memory, knowledge, workspace connectors, and native device bridges supplied by plugins

gettingStarted.intro: You can either scaffold a new project with the CLI or run the monorepo from source. The repository pins its Bun and Node versions in package.json, so install those versions first.

steps.heading: Install the CLI and scaffold a project
steps.body: The beta CLI is published as the unscoped elizaos package. Projects are deployable workspaces; plugins are reusable capability packages.
steps.code:
bun add --global elizaos@beta
elizaos create my-project --template project
elizaos create plugin-example --template plugin

steps.heading: Or run the repository from source
steps.body: bun install also prepares submodules, patches, and runtime artifacts. For a smaller development install that skips the large artifact bundle, use bun run install:light instead.
steps.code:
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/elizaos/eliza.git
cd eliza
bun install
bun run dev

steps.heading: Build, verify, and test
steps.body: The repository exposes one script per lane. bun run verify runs the package parity, dependency, type, lint, and audit gates.
steps.code:
bun run build       # build the workspace with Turbo
bun run verify      # package parity, dependency, type, lint, and audit gates
bun run test        # unit/integration lane
bun run test:e2e    # end-to-end lane
bun run cloud:mock  # local Eliza Cloud stack with mocks

steps.heading: Embed the runtime directly
steps.body: To use the runtime without the CLI or the application host, import @elizaos/core in your own TypeScript project. The scenario runner gives you executable integration coverage against a real runtime and, when configured, live models.

useCases: Build a long-running autonomous agent in TypeScript without committing to one model provider
Package a capability — a connector, a tool, a domain workflow — as a reusable plugin instead of forking an agent
Run an agent whose model calls stay on-device, using the local-inference plugin's Eliza-1 tiers
Ship an end-user agent app across web, desktop, and mobile on top of a runtime you also control in code
